            location = 3;

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I'm picking up Pokemon games with Violet and learning about every additions made to the game since gen 2, I'm having a hard time figuring out what are the Pokemon characteristics you can't change through grinding the games.</p>
<p>If I'm not mistaken, besides the Pokemon shinyness, you can now change every other aspect of your Pokemon, right? IVs are uppable with training, EVs are grindable through items and resettables with enough berries, nature can be changed with spices...</p>
<p>Is shinyness the only immutable characteristic of your Pokemon or are there others?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>As you correctly wrote, shininess is immutable.</p>
<p>But there are other properties that can't be changed:</p>
<ul>
<li>Base stats</li>
<li>Gender</li>
<li>Actual Nature (mints only change the effect of the Nature)</li>
<li><a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Characteristic" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Characteristic</a> (indicates which stat contains the highest IV)</li>
<li>Dudunsparce's form</li>
<li>Maushold's form</li>
<li>Size</li>
</ul>
<p>Most of them are related to Pokemon's <a href="https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Personality_value" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Personality value</a>, which is randomly generated and can't be changed:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>A Pokémon's personality value is an unsigned 32-bit integer that is created when the Pokémon is first generated by the game. For Pokémon encountered in the wild, it is set upon encountering them. For gift Pokémon and Eggs, it is set upon receiving them or when the Day-Care Man finds the Egg.</p>
</blockquote>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>Does it mean it can produce those goods faster, higher quality or what? Is it worth it to replace buildings with higher starred versions or prioritize going for buildings with new stuff?</p>
<p>So for example should i pick up a lumber mill to replace planks over the starter plank building or go for a bath house?</p>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>The stars correspond to the efficiency of the recipe. Unfortunately I can't find any resources online which specify the exact ratios, but I know the Lumber Mill produces about three times as many planks as the Crude Workstation for a given amount of wood, and does so considerably faster as well. So if you're low on raw materials, the improved buildings are essential. You're usually not low on wood, but planks are so important to have tons and tons of that the Lumber Mill might be worth it anyway (but the Carpenter is even better because it also has other good recipes).</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>The stars correspond to the efficiency of the recipe. Unfortunately I can't find any resources online which specify the exact ratios, but I know the Lumber Mill produces about three times as many planks as the Crude Workstation for a given amount of wood, and does so considerably faster as well. So if you're low on raw materials, the improved buildings are essential. You're usually not low on wood, but planks are so important to have tons and tons of that the Lumber Mill might be worth it anyway (but the Carpenter is even better because it also has other good recipes).</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>The stars correspond to the efficiency of the recipe. Unfortunately I can't find any resources online which specify the exact ratios, but I know the Lumber Mill produces about three times as many planks as the Crude Workstation for a given amount of wood, and does so considerably faster as well. So if you're low on raw materials, the improved buildings are essential. You're usually not low on wood, but planks are so important to have tons and tons of that the Lumber Mill might be worth it anyway (but the Carpenter is even better because it also has other good recipes).</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

            location = 3;

                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

            location = 3;

                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

            location = 3;

                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<p><strong>Minecraft Version</strong>: 1.19.3</p>
<p>I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but I'm trying to add a custom texture for a leather armour set in Minecraft via <code>customModelData</code>.</p>
<p>For some reason however, it's not working! I'm very clueless as to what I could possibly be doing wrong.</p>
<p>Here is my properties file:</p>
<pre><code>type=armor
items=leather_helmet\ leather_chestplate\ leather_leggings\ leather_boots
texture.leather_layer_1=empty
texture.leather_layer_1_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_1
texture.leather_layer_2=empty
texture.leather_layer_2_overlay=sweetheart_armor_layer_2
nbt.CustomModelData=6000
</code></pre>
<p>Here are the attached PNG layers (enlarged for improved viewing):</p>
<div class="s-table-container">
<table class="s-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/kqFJp.png" width="350"/></th>
<th><img src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/LxoYM.png" width="350"/></th>
</tr>
</thead>
</table>
</div>
<p>I have everything situated in the directory <code>~/assets/minecraft/optifine/cit/</code>. I have countless other models that work, just this one doesn't.</p>
<p>As a follow up question, what are the "overlay" elements of the properties file and are they relevant? I have tried every combination possible. Leaving overlays empty and layers defined. Leaving overlays defined and layers empty, etc etc. I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>This is older, however I wanted to go back on a save, accidentally hit ‘Restore last local saved game’ and then all my local saves got completely deleted with zero of them remaining. I luckily got my ME1 gameplay back just fine, but I want to try and get my ME2 gameplay back and the ME3 gameplay, that I was in the middle of back too.</p>
<p>I had gotten EA App earlier then reinstalled Origin afterwards finding out that wouldn’t help. Just the button to restore is grayed and there’s something there, my cloud save now says nothing for restoration, but it says under MELE that I have 114.53 KB OF 1 GB under enabling cloud save, which is selected and checked marked. (via Origin)</p>
<p>A final thing to mention, I edited my local saves with a save editor. That’s why I had said that it asked me a couple times about my saves. I’ve always said my most recently timed local saves though, if that makes a difference.
The only thing that I can find also to any form of my files when trying recovery are .lnk files, which I know also probably won’t help. ( However, nowadays nothing shows with the recovery applications. )</p>
<p>I did mess with it and it shows it not grayed out anymore, still the KB I believe? But it was reverting to the last thing that I was messing with. I also tried uninstalling and reinstalling the whole thing via Steam I believe? Didn’t help either. Didn’t touch it anymore than that for at least a month or two now.</p>
<p>So I appreciate it and thank you for any new suggestions or help that I haven’t tried yet! This will definitely be the final post since I exhausted all other resources otherwise, so thanks!</p>

<p>This is older, however I wanted to go back on a save, accidentally hit ‘Restore last local saved game’ and then all my local saves got completely deleted with zero of them remaining. I luckily got my ME1 gameplay back just fine, but I want to try and get my ME2 gameplay back and the ME3 gameplay, that I was in the middle of back too.</p>
<p>I had gotten EA App earlier then reinstalled Origin afterwards finding out that wouldn’t help. Just the button to restore is grayed and there’s something there, my cloud save now says nothing for restoration, but it says under MELE that I have 114.53 KB OF 1 GB under enabling cloud save, which is selected and checked marked. (via Origin)</p>
<p>A final thing to mention, I edited my local saves with a save editor. That’s why I had said that it asked me a couple times about my saves. I’ve always said my most recently timed local saves though, if that makes a difference.
The only thing that I can find also to any form of my files when trying recovery are .lnk files, which I know also probably won’t help. ( However, nowadays nothing shows with the recovery applications. )</p>
<p>I did mess with it and it shows it not grayed out anymore, still the KB I believe? But it was reverting to the last thing that I was messing with. I also tried uninstalling and reinstalling the whole thing via Steam I believe? Didn’t help either. Didn’t touch it anymore than that for at least a month or two now.</p>
<p>So I appreciate it and thank you for any new suggestions or help that I haven’t tried yet! This will definitely be the final post since I exhausted all other resources otherwise, so thanks!</p>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>This is older, however I wanted to go back on a save, accidentally hit ‘Restore last local saved game’ and then all my local saves got completely deleted with zero of them remaining. I luckily got my ME1 gameplay back just fine, but I want to try and get my ME2 gameplay back and the ME3 gameplay, that I was in the middle of back too.</p>
<p>I had gotten EA App earlier then reinstalled Origin afterwards finding out that wouldn’t help. Just the button to restore is grayed and there’s something there, my cloud save now says nothing for restoration, but it says under MELE that I have 114.53 KB OF 1 GB under enabling cloud save, which is selected and checked marked. (via Origin)</p>
<p>A final thing to mention, I edited my local saves with a save editor. That’s why I had said that it asked me a couple times about my saves. I’ve always said my most recently timed local saves though, if that makes a difference.
The only thing that I can find also to any form of my files when trying recovery are .lnk files, which I know also probably won’t help. ( However, nowadays nothing shows with the recovery applications. )</p>
<p>I did mess with it and it shows it not grayed out anymore, still the KB I believe? But it was reverting to the last thing that I was messing with. I also tried uninstalling and reinstalling the whole thing via Steam I believe? Didn’t help either. Didn’t touch it anymore than that for at least a month or two now.</p>
<p>So I appreciate it and thank you for any new suggestions or help that I haven’t tried yet! This will definitely be the final post since I exhausted all other resources otherwise, so thanks!</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="nofollow noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="nofollow noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="nofollow noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="nofollow noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've been playing Tetris on the virtual Game Boy console on my Nintendo Switch. As a kid, with an actual Game Boy, I remember getting to see <a href="https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jclop0AXA-4/maxresdefault.jpg" rel="noreferrer">a space shuttle launch</a> after doing well enough on an A-Type game.</p>
<p><a href="https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/gameboy/585960-tetris/faqs/8483" rel="noreferrer">This Gamespot forum guide</a> claims that this ending appears after you get more than 200,000 points. So far, I've managed about 269,000 points (getting to level 16), but I only saw <a href="http://www.kobash.com/tetris/theory/sextris_rockets.gif" rel="noreferrer">the third rocket in this image</a> launch.</p>
<p>The image states that the three rockets appear after 100,000, 150,000, and 200,000 points respectively, which matches my experience, but says nothing about the shuttle.</p>
<p>What do I have to do to get the shuttle?</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>You are playing the wrong game mode.</p>
<p>In A-TYPE, a rocket launch is shown when the player surpasses a certain score:</p>
<ul>
<li>100,000 to 149,999 points: small rocket</li>
<li>150,000 to 199,999 points: medium-sized rocket</li>
<li>200,000 or more points: big rocket</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="The small, medium, and large Tetris rocket graphics" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/0dLo1.png"/></a></p>
<p>In B-TYPE, a screen with Russian musicians and dancers is shown when completing 25 lines on level 9. The number of musicians and dancers increases with the initial height level. <strong>When completing level 9 on height 5, a Buran shuttle launch is shown additionally</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png" rel="noreferrer"><img alt="The Tetris space shuttle graphic" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/syKzO.png"/></a></p>
<p><a href="https://harddrop.com/wiki/Tetris_(Game_Boy)" rel="noreferrer">Source</a></p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>
